correctness.rationale: For any finite commutative chain ring with maximal ideal (pi) and nilpotency ell, nonzero zero-divisors of valuation i have annihilator m^(ell-i), so classes i=1..ell-1 and distinct classes i,j multiply to zero iff i+j>=ell. This is antiregular graph A_m,m=ell-1, independent of residue-field order. The recursion A_{m+2}=K1 join (K1 disjoint-union A_m), with a pendant vertex p and universal u, yields Z(A_{m+2})=Z(A_m)+1 and ready-ZF counter counts a_{m+2}=2a_m+b_m,b_{m+2}=a_m+b_m. Initial a2=2,b2=1 and a3=2,b3=2 produce Fibonacci formulas a_m=F_{m+1} for even m, =2F_{m-1} for odd m. Independently exhausted every subset of A_m for m=2..10 and confirmed Z, minimum-set counts (a_m:2,2,5,6,13,16,34,42,89), ready counts and base cases. Published theorem M(G)=Z(G) for all threshold graphs gives minrank=m-Z; ell=2 K1 exception gives Z=M=1,mr=0. No infinite inference from finite tests.
residual_risks: Only finite commutative chain rings and compressed annihilator graphs, not ordinary zero-divisor graphs or general local rings.
